A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same ReDDiT research, with matching methods, datasets, and benchmark tables. All supplied pages were inspected. v1 ends with references; v2 includes supplementary Sections 6–9 containing a proof, implementation details, dataset descriptions, and additional visual comparisons.

before.justification: v1 reports original ReDDiT enhancement results, acceleration comparisons, component and refinement-strength ablations, and efficiency measurements in Tables 1–4 and Figures 2–6.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a refinement-source ablation in Figure 6 and supplementary qualitative comparisons in Figures 9–10.

M1.justification: The operative trajectory distillation, reflectance estimation, trajectory blending, and pixel/perceptual auxiliary losses remain. v2's Corollary 1 expresses v1's Equation 9 blend using a complementary weight convention. The new residual-space analysis does not establish an additional algorithmic component or a changed training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ten datasets/subsets: LOLv1, LOLv2-real, LOLv2-synthetic, SID, SDSD, DICM, LIME, MEF, NPE, and VV. The new ablation and supplementary images use retained coverage; dataset descriptions move from v1's main text to v2's Section 8.

E2.justification: v2 newly evaluates PairLIE output as a refinement-source comparator in Figure 6. Figure 9 introduces Zero-DCE into the SID/SDSD comparisons, and Figure 10 expands the earlier Retinexformer-only unpaired visual comparison with EnGAN, Zero-DCE, and GSAD. Comparator sets in Tables 1–4 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds a refinement-source comparison using clean images, low-light inputs, PairLIE outputs, and reflectance, evaluated by PSNR at 8, 4, and 2 steps. Existing benchmark splits, preprocessing descriptions, and metrics are retained. Newly supplied training settings are disclosures, without evidence that existing experiments were changed or rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 6 adds a targeted ablation asking which refinement source best supports distillation. It compares reflectance against clean images, low-light inputs, and PairLIE outputs. The earlier component-removal and refinement-strength analyses remain as Figures 7–8.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. v2's training-iteration disclosures do not constitute uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–4 are unchanged. v2 adds refinement-source PSNR curves showing reflectance performing best and low-light inputs second, plus SID/SDSD qualitative results and additional comparator outputs for previously shown unpaired scenes. These are added findings, not improvements in retained benchmark scores.

T1.justification: v1 presents trajectory and refinement formulas without a formal supporting result. v2 Section 3.2 adds ideal-teacher assumptions, score-mismatch derivations, and a residual-space formulation in Equations 8–12. Corollary 1 establishes an algebraic refinement equivalence, with its proof supplied in supplementary Section 6.

C1.justification: v2 makes a theoretical diagnosis of fitting errors and the inference gap, together with proposed remedies, a headline contribution in the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. v1's contributions centered on ReDDiT, RATR, and empirical performance. The claims of comparable two-step performance and state-of-the-art four/eight-step results remain.

C2.justification: v1 motivates RATR through deterministic guidance and reduced fitting difficulty. v2 develops a two-factor mechanism involving score mismatch and an inference gap, interprets refinement as residual-space selection, and explains PairLIE's poorer refinement results through an unsuitable residual space. The single-step and lightweight-network limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Supplementary Section 7 supplies substantial implementation information absent from v1: SR3 teacher training, two million teacher iterations, 5,000 distillation iterations, Adam with learning rate 0.0001, EMA 0.9999, noise-schedule endpoints, patch size 96, batch size 16, and an 80GB A100 GPU. These materially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing changed settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to PairLIE, latent diffusion, and SR3, while removing the rectified-flow reference. These support the new ablation, background, and implementation disclosure. The related-work discussion and claim of the first diffusion distillation tailored to LLIE otherwise retain their positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method narrative, and conclusion are substantially rewritten around the two-factor theoretical explanation. v2 introduces numbered sections and a supplementary structure, relocates dataset descriptions, and changes the title and author block. Much of the experimental discussion remains closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 adds the conceptual overview in Figure 1, refinement-source plots in Figure 6, and supplementary Figures 9–10. It revises the pipeline display and redraws the earlier acceleration and ablation plots without their numerical subtables. Figure 10 redisplays existing unpaired examples alongside additional methods, and tables and page layout are reformatted.

improvement.justification: The new implementation details improve reproducibility, and Figure 6 supplies direct evidence for choosing reflectance over alternative refinement sources. These gains are tempered by removal of exact plot values and an unresolved weight convention: Corollary 1 weights reflectance by 1−ω, while Figure 8 treats ω as refinement strength. The main quantitative evidence remains unchanged, supporting a limited overall improvement.
